title.narrative: Honduras Early Childhood Education Improvement Project

description.narrative: The objectives of the Early Childhood Education Improvement Project for Honduras are to improve (a) Ministry of Education (SE's) institutional capacity for preschool management; (b) teaching practices of preschool teachers and Educators; and (c) physical learning environments in preschools serving children in Targeted Areas. The Project has five components. 1. Strengthening SE's Institutional Capacity for Preschool Management component will strengthen SE's key enabling conditions for sustainable preschool education management. 1.1. Development and implementation of the PEM to improve the quality of preschool education subcomponent will support the design and implementation of a PEM for preschool providers nationwide. 1.2. Promotion of community participation in preschool education subcomponent will increase community participation in preschool education as a crucial enabling condition for the successful implementation of the PEM. 1.3. Improvement of the operational, management, and technical capacity of human resources (HR) for the preschool education subsector subcomponent will support improved capacity of human resources based on the functional review of the Preschool Education Subdirectorate carried out as part of project preparation. 1.4. Improvement of the organization of SE's planning and monitoring systems subcomponent will support the development of a management framework based on quality statistical data and qualified human resources to use the available resources effectively and plan, monitor and evaluate educational services, complementing other ongoing projects and interventions in this area. 2. Updating the Curricular Design for all Preschool Service Modalities and Improving Teaching Practices in Formal Preschool Education Centers (CEPB) and Preschool Education Community Centers (CCEPREB) component will improve the quality of teaching practices in preschool classrooms by increasing the relevance of content in preschool programs, providing preschool learning materials, and supporting the implementation of improved pedagogical practices. 2.1. Upgrade of the current preschool curricular design and associated learning materials, and their provision subcomponent will support the update of the current preschool curricula design and increase articulation of curriculum design across initial education, preschool, and the first grades of basic education, to promote coherence and continuity of education service provision. 2.2. Support the implementation of improved pedagogical practices subcomponent will enhance in-service training for preschool teachers with an emphasis on the updated curricular design and learning materials. 2.3. Implementation of measurement tools for child development and the quality of learning environments subcomponent will support measurement tools to monitor and assess reforms in the preschool education subsector. 3. Improving Physical Learning Environments in Selected Preschools Serving Children in Targeted Areas component improve access to child-centered, learning-oriented, inclusive, resilient and sustainable preschool physical environments for children in targeted areas to improve equity of education outcomes. 3.1. Upgrade of building codes and infrastructure standards subcomponent will support the upgrade of building codes and infrastructure standards through the following activities. 3.2. Improvement of existing preschool physical learning environments in targeted areas will support the building, expansion and rehabilitation of learning environments of public preschools serving children in targeted areas. 4. Project Management and Evaluation component will support the strengthening of the SE's capacity to manage and oversee project implementation, as well as to monitor and evaluate project objectives and outcomes. 5. Contingency Emergency Response component will provide immediate response to eligible emergencies.

The objectives of the Project are to improve (a) SE's institutional capacity for preschool management; (b) teaching practices of preschool teachers and Educators; and (c) physical learning environments in preschools serving children in Targeted Areas.

condition.narrative: Schedule 2. Section I. A. 1. To facilitate implementation of the Project, the Recipient, through SE, shall:a) Establish, andthereafter, operate and maintain, throughout Project implementation an executive committee (the “Executive Committee”) responsiblefor Project oversight and coordination, led by SE's under-secretariat of technical-pedagogical affairs, and with the composition,functions and resources set forth in the Project Operational Manual.

Schedule 2. Section I. A. 1. To facilitate implementation of the Project, the Recipient, through SE, shall:b) Establish, andthereafter, operate and maintain, throughout Project implementation, a Project implementation unit (“PIU”) within SE, with thestaffing, functions and resources acceptable to the Association, and adequate staff, including the staff mentioned in paragraph (c)of this Section.

Schedule 2. Section I. A. 1. To facilitate implementation of the Project, the Recipient, through SE, shall:c) Without limitationof the provisions of (b) above, no later than: (i) thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, hire a Project coordinator, afinancial management specialist, and a procurement specialist; (ii) sixty (60) days after the Effective Date, hire or appoint anenvironmental specialist and a social specialist; and (iii) ninety (90) days after the Effective Date, complete the hiring of therest of the remaining staff of the PIU identified in the Project Operational Manual, all in accordance with qualifications,experience and terms of reference set forth in the Project Operational Manual.

Schedule 2. Section I. C. 1. The Recipient, through SE, shall ensure that the Project is carried out in accordance with theEnvironmental and Social Standards, in a manner acceptable to the Association.

Schedule 2. Section I. D. 1. For purposes of carrying out Parts/Components 1 and 2 of the Project, the Recipient, through SE,shall:a) No later than a hundred and twenty (120) calendar days after the Effective Date, engage an Independent VerificationAgent with qualifications and experience, and under terms of reference acceptable to the Association.

Schedule 2. Section I. D. 1. For purposes of carrying out Parts/Components 1 and 2 of the Project, the Recipient, through SE,shall:b) Cause the Independent Verification Agent to: (a) carry out each calendar semester a verification of the level ofachievement of those DLRs as set forth in the Project Operational Manual; and (b) within thirty (30) days after the end of eachcalendar semester prepare and furnish to the Recipient, through SE, Independent Verification Reports of such scope and detail asset forth in the Project Operations Manual covering the pertinent calendar semester; and

Schedule 2. Section I. D. 1. For purposes of carrying out Parts/Components 1 and 2 of the Project, the Recipient, through SE,shall:c) Furnish a copy of each Independent Verification Report to the Association, no later than forty-five (45) days after theend of each calendar semester.

title.narrative: 1. Preschool Education Quality Model (PEQM) implemented at school-level (Depth indicator)

comment.narrative: The PEQM, including the pilot and a field instrument for monitoring progress, was finalized and formally approved by the MoE in January 2025. A socialization strategy is in place.

title.narrative: 2. Participating preschool teachers and Educators with satisfactory teaching practices

comment.narrative: The Certificate in Pedagogical Skills for preschool Teachers and Educators was completed from May to October 2025 and consisted of five modules delivered through in-person and virtual workshops, virtual classroom activities, and both virtual and in-person mentoring sessions. However, results from the TEACH ECE endline show that only 42% of participants demonstrate satisfactory teaching practices.

title.narrative: 3. Classrooms of preschool education centers in Targeted Areas with physical environments that meet quality conditions to promote learning

comment.narrative: Infrastructure works under Phase I in 64 classrooms (52 preschool education centers) were completed in November 2024 in the departments of Copán, El Paraiso, Lempira, and Olancho. Under Phase II, works in Yoro were completed in August 2025, delivering 20 classrooms (14 preschool centers). In Gracias a Dios, 17 classrooms (14 preschool centers) are on track to be completed by end January 2026.

title.narrative: IRI 1: PEQM approved and implemented at school level (Breadth indicator)

target.value: PEQM implemented in public preschools across the country (at least 25% of public preschools are carrying out at least 20% of the PEQM dimensions)

comment.narrative: The PEQM, including the pilot and a field instrument for monitoring progress, was finalized and formally approved by the MoE in January 2025. A socialization strategy is in place.

actual.value: PEQM officially approved by MoE. PEQM piloted in selected preschool centers.

title.narrative: IRI 2: Strengthened Preschool education community networks and Activities carried out in Targeted Departments

baseline.value: No accredited Preschool education community networks

target.value: All of the Preschool education community networks in the 6 most disadvantaged departments trained in the Strengthening Program

comment.narrative: MoE completed three monitoring visits. Of 110 networks, 63% (69) finalized all phases; 17% (19) are in progress; 20% (22) have not started due to political, staffing, or climate constraints.

actual.value: 110 “Preschool education Community Networks” from the project 6 target Departments (Olancho, Copan, Yoro, El Paraiso, Gracias a Dios y Lempira) were trained in the Strengthening Program, which represent 100% “Preschool education Community Networks”.

title.narrative: IRI 10: Pre-investment education infrastructure studies for preschool developed

comment.narrative: The pre-investment studies for 253 preschool education centers (300 preschool classrooms) have been completed for the 6 most disadvantaged departments of Honduras (Copán, El Paraiso, Gracias a Dios, Lempira, Olancho and Yoro).

title.narrative: IRI 3: Strengthened human resource capacity for preschool education management at the central and departmental levels

baseline.value: Functional Review including assessment of organizational structure and capacity of the human resources for preschool management.

target.value: Strengthening of the SDGEPB with the hiring of 7 technical staff at the central level and 18 Heads of Preschool Education in the 18 departments. Design and official approval by SE of a sustainable and long-term human resources strategy for public preschool teachers and Educators.

comment.narrative: DLR 3.1 has been achieved. For DLRs 3.2–3.3, five hires are in place (2 central, 3 decentralized), but recruitment continues to face structural and financial constraints. Dialogue between SE and SEFIN on 20 pending positions will continue, with prioritization recommended for the next administration. The DLR 3.5 consultancy is underway, targeting completion by February 2026.

actual.value: The MoE authorities completed the review of contracting agreements, budgets, and other administrative procedures that fulfill this indicator

title.narrative: IRI 8: Certified preschool teachers and Educators

target.value: Design and official approval of a Preschool Teacher and Educator Training Program/Certificate. 2,000 preschool teachers and Educators enrolled and attending training program. 1,300 teachers and educators certified in the teacher training program.

comment.narrative: The Certificate design was completed in May 2025, and teachers and educators participated in the training modules from mid-May to October 2025.

actual.value: Design and official approval of a Preschool Teacher and Educator Training Program/Certificate. 2,000 preschool teachers and Educators enrolled and attending training program. The final number of teachers and educators who successfully obtained certification is still pending confirmation.

title.narrative: IRI 7: Centers with adequate learning materials

comment.narrative: The distribution of 6,200 educational kits to the 18 Departmental Directorates of Education has been completed. Delivery to schools will managed by preschool education coordinators and is expected to be completed by December 2025.

title.narrative: IRI 6: Centers with the adequate amount of curricular tools

comment.narrative: In the last quarter of CY23, 196,000 workbooks were printed for second and third grade preschool education and distributed to the 18 Departmental Education Directorates. By the start of the academic year in February 2024, all workbooks were distributed to 100% CEPB and CCEPREB classrooms. A new printing and distribution process is underway, including workbooks, formative assessments, guides, and emergent literacy materials.

title.narrative: IRI 15. Number of teachers and Educators trained on adaptation measures for climate change within the In-service Teacher and Educator Training Program

comment.narrative: The Certificate program carried out from mid-May to October 2025 included content on adaptation measures for climate change.

title.narrative: IRI 14. Number of teachers and Educators trained on gender-appropriate pedagogy within the In-service Teacher and Educator Training Program

comment.narrative: The Certificate program carried out from mid-May to October 2025 included content on gender pedagogy.

title.narrative: IRI 16. Number of teachers and Educators trained on prevention measures for school crime and violence within the In-service Teacher and Educator Training Program

comment.narrative: The Certificate program carried out from mid-May to October 2025 included content on prevention measures for school crime and violence.

title.narrative: IRI 9: Preschool teachers and Educators that receive in-service training focused on pedagogical practices

comment.narrative: A new implementation strategy has been developed for the training plan to ensure effective pedagogical training for teachers and educators. Additionally, the MoE has proposed a complementary training plan for preschool teachers and educators. To date, the MoE has reported that 2,645 of the 12,000 teachers and educators at this education level have received training in pedagogical practices.

title.narrative: IRI 12: Centers in targeted municipalities selected based on the targeting criteria

comment.narrative: 253 preschool education centers (approximately 300 preschool classrooms) have been selected in 45 municipalities of the 6 most disadvantaged departments of Honduras (Copán, El Paraiso, Gracias a Dios, Lempira, Olancho y Yoro) to carry out pre-investment studies.

A new implementation strategy has been developed for the training plan to ensure effective pedagogical training for teachers and educators. Additionally, the MoE has proposed a complementary training plan for preschool teachers and educators. To date, the MoE has reported that 2,645 teachers and educators at this education level have received training in pedagogical practices.

title.narrative: IRI 11: Number of training workshops held on school maintenance in beneficiary schools.

comment.narrative: Maintenance training workshops for all 52 preschool centers (64 classrooms) under Phase I were completed in the second quarter of CY2025. Workshops for Phase II are planned for March 2026.

title.narrative: IRI 13. Citizen Engagement Indicator: PEQM - Teacher satisfaction survey – feedback received informs the future implementation of the PEQM

comment.narrative: The teacher satisfaction survey is expected to be completed by the closing date, with fieldwork expected to begin by second trimester 2026.

title.narrative: IRI 5: Revision and improvement of the curricular tools, and learning materials

comment.narrative: To date, the Project has updated selected curricular tools and defined the process for the printing and distribution of curricular tools, which is expected to be completed by the closing date.

title.narrative: Students supported with better education, in early childhood education

comment.narrative: By February 2024, 196,000 second- and third-grade preschool children had received workbooks.

title.narrative: Students benefiting from direct interventions to enhance learning

comment.narrative: By February 2024, 196,000 second- and third-grade preschool children had received workbooks.

title.narrative: IRI 4: Staff of the Management Planning and Evaluation Unit (UPEG) at the central and decentralized levels and other units trained in planning and public administration

comment.narrative: The Strategic Planning and Public Administration Diploma for capacity building for the MoE Management Planning and Evaluation Unit (UPEG) has been completed, with more than 100 central and decentralized level technicians trained to improve organizational performance within the MoE.
